key_insight: Low held-out force error does not guarantee stable molecular dynamics for semiconductor nanocrystals; dynamical robustness depends strongly on the MLIP architecture and refinement strategy.
engineering_relevance: For nanocrystal simulation workflows, model selection should prioritize long-timescale stability and uncertainty-guided testing, not just validation accuracy.
method: Benchmarked 5 graph-neural-network MLIPs: SchNet, PaiNN, NequIP, Allegro, and MACE
Used a chloride-passivated CdSe nanocluster (149 atoms) trained on 1,000 DFT configurations and tested on 2,000 held-out configurations
Evaluated force accuracy, computational cost, uncertainty, and 1 ns molecular dynamics stability at 300 K
evidence_signal: Allegro had the lowest validation force MAE (12–14 meV/Å), while SchNet had the highest (84–110 meV/Å), yet only NequIP was stable for 1 ns without extra data and MACE became stable only after adding 34 active-learning configurations.
watch_item: Active-learning gains were highly architecture dependent, so low error metrics or small data additions may still fail to produce stable surface-dominated nanostructure dynamics.
paper_title: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials for Dynamical Stability in Inorganic Semiconductor Nanocrystals: A CdSe Case Study
